'''''Cibotium glaucum''''', the '''hāpu‘u pulu''', is a species of fern in the family [[Cyatheaceae]], native to Hawaii.<ref name="CIGL" >{{cite web |url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=CIGL |title=''Cibotium glaucum'' (Sm.) Hook. & Arn. |last1=Marcus |first1=Joseph A. |date=8 May 2015 |website=Plant Database |publisher=Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center |access-date=11 November 2023 |quote=Hawaiian Tree Fern, Hapu'U Pulu, Blonde Tree Fern, Female Tree Fern }}</ref><ref name="POWO_17069480-1" >{{cite POWO |id=17069480-1 |title=''Cibotium glaucum'' (Sm.) Hook. & Arn. |access-date=11 November 2023 }}</ref> A slow-growing [[tree fern]] typically {{cvt|6|to|10|ft|0}} tall but reaching {{cvt|25|ft|m|0}}, it is hardy in [[Hardiness zone|USDA zones]] 10 through 12.<ref name="MBG_285722" >{{cite web |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285722 |title=''Cibotium glaucum'' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2023 |website=Plant Finder |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=11 November 2023 }}</ref><ref name="CIGL" /> Its fiddleheads are the source of the material [[Pulu (material)|pulu]], which means "mulch" or "padding" in the [[Hawaiian language]].<ref name="pulu">{{Hawaiian Dictionaries |pulu |accessdate=20 October 2010 }}</ref> Women used pulu as an absorbent during their [[menstrual cycle]]s.<ref>{{Hawaiian Dictionaries |pe'a |exact=yes |accessdate=20 October 2010 }}</ref>
